summary: A State of the Union opens from a trouble the whole country shares (a war, a danger abroad, a disaster) before any report.
realLife: Three of the six addresses read began from a shared trouble: Roosevelt in 1944 on the war, Eisenhower in 1958 on dangers abroad, Reagan in 1986 on the Challenger loss.
sources: Read Nov 24, 2026: the first and last paragraphs of each address on the Presidency Project page; the middles were not read.
inGame: Section `story` and the year's disaster row (`the-disaster`); needs: the occasion section to open on the disaster instead of the report move.

turns.what: Opens on a good year's result, not a trouble.
turns.writesBack: The paper opens on the good news.

turns.what: The trouble is named in a clause, then the report goes on.
turns.writesBack: The listener hears it as one fact among others.
